headline: Asia: Russian strikes kill 24 across Ukraine after Zelensky warning
script:
Good afternoon. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- Asia: Russian strikes kill 24 across Ukraine after Zelensky warning.
- South Asia: US Vice President Vance says Iran must cut enrichment to end war.
- Western Russia: Families with children and police veteran: what is known about those killed in Russian strike on Pryluky.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
The Caribbean - bottom line: Former Air J plane bombed in Iran - Pilot recalls good times flying ‘Mike Papa’ from Jamaica to UK, wants reintroduction of national airline.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 12 hours ago: Former Air J plane bombed in Iran - Pilot recalls good times flying ‘Mike Papa’ from Jamaica to UK, wants reintroduction of national airline.
When the Israeli Air Force reported the destruction of Iran’s presidential VIP Airbus A340-300 often dubbed ‘Iran Force One’ during a military strike in Iran in March of this year, the repercussions were felt beyond the Middle East, reaching Kingston, Jamaica. The long-range jet was once in the fleet of the now-defunct Air Jamaica. And for veteran aircraft pilot Edward Miller, who regularly captained the airplane on flights from Jamaica to London and Manchester in the United Kingdom, news of its demise hit a personal chord.
United States - bottom line: Army sets date, location for execution of Nidal Malik Hasan.
- Military Times, 4 hours ago: Army sets date, location for execution of Nidal Malik Hasan.
The execution by firing squad of Hasan is scheduled for Dec. 3 at Fort Hood, the same location where the former Army officer killed 13 and wounded 32.
- Military Times, 4 hours ago: Latest AH-64 Apache grounding likely to last months, officials say.
An order to ground hundreds of the Army’s AH-64E Apache attack helicopters is likely to affect every squadron and is expected to be in place for months.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America - bottom line: Lionel Messi receives UBA honorary doctorate before final national team match.
- Buenos Aires Herald, 21 hours ago: Lionel Messi receives UBA honorary doctorate before final national team match.
The Argentine football superstar called the distinction ‘an honor,’ adding that it was awarded to him on a ‘very special day’ La entrada Lionel Messi receives UBA honorary doctorate before final national team match se publicó primero en Buenos Aires Herald.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: Families with children and police veteran: what is known about those killed in Russian strike on Pryluky.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 4 hours ago: Families with children and police veteran: what is known about those killed in Russian strike on Pryluky.
Russian forces attacked Pryluky in Chernihiv Oblast with six missiles on the morning of 7 October. One of the missiles hit a five-storey apartment building, destroying two sections. So far, 16 people are known to have been killed and 55 injured. Rescue workers are still clearing the rubble.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 5 hours ago: EU calls strikes on commercial vessels in Black Sea unacceptable.
European Commission officials condemned Russian strikes on merchant vessels in the Black Sea, warning that the attacks threaten international maritime security.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 3 hours ago: Russian missiles hit cardboard and paper mill in Kyiv Oblast.
Russian missiles have struck the production and warehouse facilities of the Kyiv Cardboard and Paper Mill in Obukhiv, Kyiv Oblast, forcing the plant to halt operations.
- The Moscow Times, 8 hours ago: Russia Drops Criminal Case Against Children’s Hospice Founder Lida Moniava.
Moniava had been charged with spreading “false information” about Russia’s army for a post about Ukrainian civilians killed in Russian attacks.
Southern Europe - bottom line: Serbian Student Targeted by Spyware Attack Sues Authorities.
- Balkan Insight, one day ago: Serbian Student Targeted by Spyware Attack Sues Authorities.
Lawyers for one of 14 people targeted by Pegasus spyware file criminal complaint against Serbian intelligence agency officials, police and the Israeli company behind the surveillance technology after institutions fail to react.
- Balkan Insight, one day ago: Kosovo Protesters Against Hague Court Gather Again After Clashes.
After violent clashes on Monday night, protesters started to reassemble in Pristina to demand legal changes to curb the powers of the Kosovo Specialist Chambers war crimes court following convictions of guerrilla leaders.
- Balkan Insight, one day ago: Bulgarian PM and Opposition Quarrel Over Black Sea Drone Attack.
Kremlin-friendly PM condemns attack on two international cargo ships in Bulgarian waters as 'crude violation of law' – but opposition criticises him for not pointing finger at Moscow.
- Balkan Insight, one day ago: Kosovo Political Leaders Trade Blame as Another Election Looms.
New election likely as political parties fail to agree on electing a president and protesters keep up pressure for adoption of law curbing powers of Kosovo Specialist Chambers, following its conviction of wartime guerrilla leaders.

AFRICA
Persian Gulf Region - bottom line: WATCH: IDF destroys house of terrorist who killed Netanel Chkroun in West Bank terror attack.
- Jerusalem Post, just now: WATCH: IDF destroys house of terrorist who killed Netanel Chkroun in West Bank terror attack.
Meanwhile, the IDF carried out a strike killing two Hamas terrorists who stored explosives in Gaza's Kamal Adwan Hospital, one of whom worked as a "civil defense worker."
- Jerusalem Post, just now: British Airways resumes Tel Aviv flights for first time since February.
The airline has not operated on the route since Israel launched Operation Roaring Lion, carrying out airstrikes on Iran, on February 28.
- Jerusalem Post, just now: Mamdani: Suffering did not begin, end on October 7, continued throughout Israel's 'Gaza genocide'.
Mayor Zohran Mamdani mourned those killed and abducted on October 7 while accusing Israel of genocide, apartheid, and war crimes during the Israel-Hamas War and the Gaza ceasefire.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 6 hours ago: Israeli attacks across Gaza kill at least four Palestinians.
Israeli air strike kills Palestinian Civil Defence rescue volunteer in northern Gaza.
Africa - bottom line: Israelis mourn October 7 attack as Palestinians in Gaza live in ruins of war.
- Africanews, ABC News Australia, 6 hours ago: Israelis mourn October 7 attack as Palestinians in Gaza live in ruins of war.
Israelis are gathering Wednesday to commemorate the third anniversary of the October 7 attack that killed 1,200 people and saw 251 taken hostage. In Gaza, the territory's almost two million people live in ruins.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 13 hours ago: Sudan: Sudan's Death Toll in 2025 Could Be As High As 100,000 - How We Did the Count.
[The Conversation Africa] Estimates of the number of people directly killed in Sudan's civil war vary widely, in part because counting casualties in active conflict zones is extremely difficult. In 2025, for instance, one conflict monitoring organisation reported around 19,000 direct deaths from political violence across Sudan. Other research teams put the toll at more than 70,000.
- Africanews, 21 hours ago: Tigray drone strikes continue as life resumes in Mekelle.
Government-allied forces say they are using drones against Tigray fighters, while markets and local transport are slowly returning to the streets of the regional capital.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 7 hours ago: Nigeria: Jubilation As Troops Neutralise Iswap Commander, Many Terrorists Planning Attack.
[Daily Trust] A cross-section of Nigerians have lauded troops over their recent exploits where they neutralized a senior leader of the Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP).
South Africa - bottom line: South Africa: Eastern Cape Orders New R1.6-Billion Textbooks As Western Cape Holds Back.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 2 hours ago: South Africa: Eastern Cape Orders New R1.6-Billion Textbooks As Western Cape Holds Back.
[GroundUp] Basic education minister Siviwe Gwarube has endorsed the controversial catalogue for grade 1 to 3 learning materials
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 9 hours ago: Zimbabwe: Fake Weather Alert Sparks Flood Panic in Harare.
[263Chat] The Meteorological Services Department (MSD) has dismissed a weather warning circulating on social media saying it was not issued by the department.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 10 hours ago: South Africa: Medical Negligence Costs Billions, but SA Still Can't Measure Patient Harm.
[Health-e] Medico-legal liabilities stand at R57.6-billion. SA cannot reliably measure patient harm. Staff shortages and missed warning signs put patients at risk.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 11 hours ago: Zimbabwe: Wreckage From Chivayo Helicopter Crash Moved for Forensic Examination - Report Expected Within 30 Days.
[New Zimbabwe] INVESTIGATIONS into the helicopter crash that killed businessman Wicknell Chivayo, his wife Lucy Muteke and three others have entered the forensic examination phase, with government expecting a preliminary report in 30 days.

ASIA
Asia - bottom line: Russian strikes kill 24 across Ukraine after Zelensky warning.
- South China Morning Post - China, The Moscow Times, ABC News Australia, one hour ago: Russian strikes kill 24 across Ukraine after Zelensky warning.
At least 24 people were killed in Russian strikes across Ukraine on Wednesday, including four young children who died when a missile slammed into a residential block in the north of the country as they slept. Windows shattered in the powerful blast in Pryluky, in the Chernihiv region, reducing one half of the five-storey building into a smoking pile of charred concrete and twisted metal. President Volodymyr Zelensky said three of the 18 victims of the strike were just 12 months old while another...
- South China Morning Post - China, The Hindu - International, 7 hours ago: Israel marks 3 years since October 7 attack that sparked war in Gaza.
Israel marked the third anniversary of Hamas’ October 7 attack on Wednesday with silent tributes, new strikes on Gaza and intense political debate, weeks before elections in which the country’s deadliest day will be front and centre. At the site of the Nova music festival, where Hamas militants in trucks and paragliders opened fire around dawn on October 7, 2023, family members bowed their heads in silence – although at least one instead put on techno music in tribute to the dead. Both at Nova...
- South China Morning Post - China, The Hindu - International, just now: Yemen’s Houthis attack Aden airport as fighting intensifies.
⁠Yemen’s Houthis attacked Aden’s international airport with ballistic missiles and explosive-laden drones on Wednesday, the country’s transport ministry said, as fighting between the Iran-aligned group and Saudi-backed government forces intensified. Fighting has been focused in recent days on areas around the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a shipping route that has become more crucial for energy exports since the conflict between the US and Iran restricted trade through the Strait of Hormuz. This week,...
- Taipei Times, just now: Mourning, war and elections as Israel marks anniversary of Oct. 7 attacks.
South Asia - bottom line: US Vice President Vance says Iran must cut enrichment to end war.
- Dawn (Pakistan), The Hindu - International, 13 hours ago: US Vice President Vance says Iran must cut enrichment to end war.
US Vice President JD Vance has said in an exclusive interview with Reuters that Iran must make a meaningful reduction in its nuclear enrichment capacity to satisfy US demands and end the country’s seven-month war, even as Washington was unsure how Tehran makes decisions in negotiations. Vance, a longtime sceptic of US involvement in foreign wars, has taken a leading role in negotiating a settlement to the conflict and brokered a provisional peace agreement in June that quickly fell apart.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 6 hours ago: In pictures: What Gaza looks like after 3 years of destruction wrought by Israel.
Three years after Hamas’s Oct 7, 2023 attack on Israel triggered a devastating onslaught, much of Gaza still lies in ruins. Deadly Israeli strikes continue despite a fragile ceasefire that has largely held for almost a year. Homes, hospitals, schools and entire neighbourhoods have been destroyed or severely damaged, while millions of Palestinians have been displaced. Here is a look at the scale of destruction and what life — rather, what remains of it — is like in Gaza today.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 9 hours ago: 18 terrorists killed in separate engagements in KP, Balochistan: state media.
Security forces eliminated 18 terrorists in separate engagements in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan, state media reported on Wednesday, citing security sources. In KP, Pakistan TV reported that security forces “killed 13 Fitna al-Khawarij terrorists in an intelligence-based operation in North Waziristan, as operations against militant groups continue under the Azm-e-Istehkam vision”. Separately, in Balochistan’s Mastung district, security forces killed five terrorists belonging to Fitna al-Hindustan, Pakistan TV reported.
- Dawn (Pakistan), The Hindu - International, South China Morning Post - China, 2 hours ago: 7 cops injured as police checkpost comes under attack in KP's Kohat.
PESHAWAR: Seven policemen were injured when terrorists attacked a police checkpost in Kohat early on Wednesday. “The attack was successfully repulsed. The injured cops are safe,” a senior police official, who requested to remain anonymous, told Dawn. According to police sources, the policemen were injured after terrorists hurled a hand grenade at the checkpost located in the jurisdiction of the Gombat police station. The injured were shifted to hospital, where their condition was stated to be out of danger, the sources added.
India - bottom line: Tanker attacks in Strait of Hormuz highest in a week since Iran war began: Report.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 2 hours ago: Tanker attacks in Strait of Hormuz highest in a week since Iran war began: Report.
Last week, attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz reached a high level of activity. There were at least twelve incidents reported involving various types of vessels. This surge coincides with Gulf producers increasing their oil exports significantly. The International Maritime Organisation also reported nine separate incidents during the same timeframe. Overall, these developments cast doubts on the stability and security of maritime operations in the region.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 3 hours ago: What is military exemption? Why South Korea weighs cuts after Asian Games backlash.
Following inflammatory comments from football players, South Korea is rethinking its policy on military service exemptions for athletes. This reevaluation comes amidst public outcry over the equity of the existing regulations. Culture and Sports Minister Chae Hwi-young noted a shift in societal attitudes towards military service, leading the Defence Ministry to explore removing additional service requirements for athletes.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 5 hours ago: From the 'Promised Land' to Oct 7 attack: Origin story of Israel-Palestine conflict.

For individuals who receive a CAS, this means information on their mutual funds, stocks and, going forward, fixed deposits (FDs) can be viewed together in one place. The change will allow demat account holders to see details of their demat holdings as well as bank deposit accounts together in a single CAS.

- NK News, 9 hours ago: Seoul seeks joint probe with UN Command into North Korean border crossings.
South Korea plans to investigate North Korean incursions across the Military Demarcation Line (MDL) in order to formally declare them violations of the Korean War armistice, Seoul’s Defense Ministry said Wednesday, following the Sept. 21 mine explosion that injured three ROK soldiers. Australia - bottom line: Tensions escalate in Middle East as Houthis target airports.
- ABC News Australia, 11 hours ago: Tensions escalate in Middle East as Houthis target airports.
